en.title: Most Frequently Booked Hotel Room
en.description:
The hotel has floors 0..9, and each floor has rooms A..Z. + means a booking and − means a checkout. The sequence is valid, and all rooms are initially free. Output the room with the most cumulative bookings (checkouts are not counted); on ties, choose the lexicographically smallest room.

The input/output and examples are compiled by CSWork; numeric ranges marked as this site's are this site's judging conventions.
en.input: The first line contains n (1..600), followed by n lines of three-character records, such as +0A or -0A; each room is guaranteed to be free before every booking and booked before every checkout.
en.output: Output the answer required by the problem.
en.explanation: Example 1: 1A is booked twice and 0B once, so the output is 1A. Example 2: each room is booked once, and 0A is lexicographically smaller. Example 3: 1A has two cumulative bookings, more than the one for 0A; the final occupancy of the rooms is not what is compared.
hints: Count only the rooms in + records, and pick the best room by booking count in descending order, then by room name in ascending order.
